requestKey: How do I plan outfits from my own wardrobe?|cherly.app|sample0

payload.text:
Here’s a simple, repeatable way to plan great outfits using what you already own.

Quick start (today)
1) Pull favorites: Grab 10–15 pieces you actually wear (tops, bottoms, 1–2 layers, 2 shoes).  
2) Pick a palette: Choose 2 neutrals (e.g., black, navy) + 1–2 accent colors you like.  
3) Make “formulas”: Pair items into 5 outfits using simple silhouettes (see below). Snap photos. Wear this week.

A step‑by‑step system
1) Inventory your wardrobe
- Try-on session (60–90 min). Keep only items that fit, feel good, and suit your life now.
- Make three piles: Keep (fits/you love), Tailor (specific fixes), Let go (worn out/never reach for).
- Note “workhorse” pieces (the ones you always grab). These decide your style direction.

2) Define your lifestyle split
- Estimate your week in percentages: Work/School, Casual, Going out, Formal, Exercise, Home.
- Plan outfits in proportion to those buckets. Example: if 60% is casual, most looks should be casual-smart.

3) Build mix-and-match “clusters”
- Start with 5 pieces that all work together: 2 tops + 2 bottoms + 1 layer. Aim for each top to match both bottoms.
- Add 2 shoes and 1–2 bags that match the palette. This single cluster can yield ~8–12 outfits.
- Make 2–3 clusters for your main seasons; share colors so clusters cross‑pair.

4) Use reliable outfit formulas
- Slim top + wide leg bottom + structured shoe.
- Oversized top + slim bottom + sleek sneaker/boot.
- Monochrome base (top+bottom) + contrasting third piece (blazer/cardigan).
- Dress or jumpsuit + tailored layer + statement shoe.
- Tee + straight jeans + third piece (trench/denim jacket) + clean sneaker/loafer.
Tip: Repeat a color at least twice in the outfit (e.g., shoe = belt; bag = print color) to look intentional.

5) Plan your week in 15 minutes
- Check your calendar and the weather for the next 5–7 days.
- Slot outfits by day and occasion; front‑load your favorite/most polished looks for busy days.
- Lay items on a rack or save mirror photos in a “This Week” album.
- Prep accessories and underlayers (tights/socks/bras) so you can dress fast.

Weekly planner template (copy/paste)
- Mon: Event/Temp: __ / Outfit: Top __, Bottom __, Layer __, Shoes __, Bag __, Accessory __
- Tue: …
- Backups: 1 smart-casual look, 1 comfort look.

6) Photo lookbook
- Take mirror pics of every outfit you like. Tag by season, occasion, and vibe (e.g., “sharp,” “creative,” “low‑effort”).
- On low-energy days, just pick from the album.

7) Color and texture rules that simplify choices
- Palette: 2–3 neutrals + 2 accents + 1 favorite print.
- Textures: mix one smooth (silk/cotton poplin) with one textured (denim/knit/tweed) to add depth.
- Metals: stick to mostly one metal (gold or silver) per outfit for cohesion.

8) Fit and proportion cheats
- If the top is loose, choose a fitted bottom (and vice versa).
- Cropped or tucked tops lengthen legs with high-rise bottoms.
- Add a third piece (blazer, cardigan, vest) to “finish” casual bases.

9) Shoes and accessories = outfit changers
- Keep 1 smart shoe, 1 casual sneaker, 1 boot, 1 fun/statement shoe in your main season.
- Belts define shape; scarves/hats add color; watches/earrings polish quickly.
- Match formality levels: athletic shoes with tailored pieces? Balance with a structured coat/bag.

10) Maintenance and editing
- End of week: note what you didn’t wear and why (fit, comfort, color, duplication).
- Create a tiny tailor/clean/repair list so more pieces become wearable.
- “Rule of 3” before buying anything new: it must make 3 outfits with items you already own.

Low-effort options
- Two-uniform approach: pick 2 favorite formulas and rotate different colors/shoes.
- 5x5 mini-capsule: 5 tops x 5 bottoms in one palette gives you a month of unique combos.

Common pitfalls to avoid
- Too many “orphans” (items that match nothing). Fix with a linking color or neutral basics.
- Ignoring underlayers and shoes—these decide comfort and polish.
- Planning looks that don’t match your actual week, climate, or laundry cycle.

If you want, tell me:
- Your climate and typical week, any dress code, favorite colors/prints, and 3 items you love wearing.
I can map a custom palette, 2–3 outfit formulas, and a ready-to-wear week from what you already have. If you’d like, you can also upload a few wardrobe photos and I’ll help build clusters.
